einstellungen.text: You're counting mistakes. And your dad is waiting in the last row.
Tomorrow morning, one hour before the opening. You go through your checklist.
Forty-seven items. Lights. Sound. Signs. Every check mark calms you down for a second.
The rows of chairs are still empty. You walk them and check every seat. Lights on the chairs. Cables on the floor.
All the way in the back sits your dad. Still in his gray work jacket.
He drives a bus. Today he left work early. Just for you.
He's holding a thermos in his lap. He's been sitting there for twenty minutes.
Twenty minutes. And you didn't see him. Only your list. Item by item.
"I didn't want to be in the way."
At school events, your dad is always like this. Quiet. In the back. Like he's too much.
You close the list. Five minutes. You sit down next to him.
He pours you peppermint tea. It smells like your kitchen.
Then he reaches into his jacket pocket. He hesitates.
He sets an old ticket in your lap. "I was there last time too."
